transcript.answer: The OpenTelemetry metrics API, unlike its tracing API, has no proxy meter. An instrument created from `metrics.getMeter()` before a `MeterProvider` is registered is therefore a permanent no-op. It stays a no-op even if a provider is registered later. In Lore, `libs/server-core/src/outbound/otel.ts` created its instruments at import time. The entrypoint imported that file before `initOtel()` ran, so counters such as `lore.http.requests` and `lore.tool.calls` never recorded anything. The fix (ADR-050, PR #2652) moved the instruments to `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts`. There they are looked up lazily on the current global meter provider at record time, memoized per provider.

judgements.reason: The answer states that the metrics API has no proxy meter, that pre-registration instruments stay no-ops permanently, and that Lore resolves instruments lazily against the current provider, matching all essentials of the gold answer.
